source.title: Dopamine neurons encode the better option in rats deciding between differently delayed or sized rewards

confidence_rationale: Strong single-unit electrophysiology from VTA dopamine neurons in rats performing a delay/magnitude choice task. The load-bearing finding for this lit-pull: VTA-DA cue-evoked activity initially reflected the *better* option (the one with higher subjective value) even when the rat subsequently selected a different option. Mapped to REE, this is direct neural evidence for a dopaminergic readiness signal over a leading candidate that is upstream of the commit decision -- the system can represent 'the better option is X and I am preparing it' before commitment, and commitment can fire on a different option only by overriding that preparation. The implication for REE: there is an empirically grounded readiness/value signal whose state at the moment of commit-entry distinguishes 'I committed because the prepared plan was ready' from 'I committed because the world stopped surprising me'. The current rv-only predicate is blind to this distinction. Confidence is moderate-to-high but not maximal: the paper is about choice between two known options rather than about commitment versus exploration, and the framing 'premature-commit pathology' is the user's framing of an associated literature rather than a primary claim of this specific paper. The paper anchors a body of Roesch / Schoenbaum work where impulsive choice phenotypes (premature commit) map onto dysregulated DA readiness signals; this entry is the cleanest single load-bearing finding from that body of work.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Single-unit recordings from putative dopamine neurons in rat ventral tegmental area (VTA) during a behavioural task in which the rat chose between two odour-cued options differing in reward delay or reward size. As expected, DA firing on reward delivery reflected prediction error. The novel finding: cue-evoked DA firing came to reflect the value of the better option even on trials when the rat subsequently chose the worse option, indicating that DA encodes a value/readiness signal over the leading candidate that is dissociable from the action ultimately selected. The result generalises across delay-discounting and size-discounting manipulations.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-090 gates committed-mode entry on `running_variance < commitment_threshold`. The Roesch et al. finding establishes that biological action systems carry a DA-encoded readiness/value signal over the leading candidate that is informationally distinct from any precision-of-prediction signal. A commitment that fires when this readiness signal is *absent or low* (as in V3-EXQ-592 seed 42, where nav_competence=0.0) is mechanistically unlike biological commit-entry, which is downstream of the readiness signal. Beyond this specific paper, the wider Roesch / Schoenbaum / Schultz body of work links *premature-commit pathology* (impulsive choice, addiction, OCD-style early closure) to dysregulation of this DA readiness signal. Mapping the V3-EXQ-592 trajectory onto that pathology axis: an rv-only predicate that lets the agent commit without a readiness signal is *pre-pathological* by design -- it implements premature commit as the baseline, not the failure mode.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper is about choice between two known, cued options, not about commitment versus exploration in a novel environment. The translation 'DA encodes readiness over the leading candidate, so a commit gate should reference that readiness' is the architectural transfer; the paper does not directly test commit-entry gating. The 'premature-commit pathology' framing draws on the broader Roesch / Schoenbaum corpus (impulsivity, addiction, OCD-style early closure) -- one paper carries the architectural anchor but not the full pathology mapping. Subsequent papers in that body of work (and Watanabe / Sakagami parallel cohorts) would strengthen the pathology side; this entry establishes the load-bearing neural finding.
mapping.source_context: Adult male Long-Evans rats (n=6) trained on an odour-cued choice task with two reward wells. Conditions manipulated relative delay (short vs long) or relative size (small vs large) between the two wells. Single-unit recordings from putative VTA dopamine neurons (identified by waveform + response properties); 81 neurons recorded. Analysis used standard PSTH + ANOVA + apomorphine pharmacological confirmation of DA identity in a subset.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: Nat Neurosci, single-unit DA recording with pharmacological identity confirmation, well-controlled choice task. Mapping fidelity moderate: the architectural claim transfers (DA carries readiness/value over the leading candidate, distinct from precision) but the specific behavioural test is choice between two known options rather than commit-vs-explore. Transfer risk modest-to-high: rat -> generalised-vertebrate is well-trodden for VTA-DA function, but the 'premature-commit pathology' framing draws on a broader corpus than this paper alone. The weakens direction is on the rv-only predicate: a substrate that licenses commit without a readiness signal implements as baseline what biological systems treat as pathology.
